attempts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Render a 4-column 2-row sheet of EIGHT successive walking-animation frames. Pure SOLID WHITE background, no grid, no text. Image1 is the exact NORTHWEST CAMERA/character/painting reference: a lumberjack viewed FROM BEHIND walking AWAY toward screen UPPER LEFT, broad olive-green back visible, nose barely visible at LEFT of head. Image2 is ONLY leg animation reference; reproduce its alternating leg halves and distinct narrow passing poses but turn the animation to the northwest view of image1.
Identity locked: orange stitched cap, brown hair and short beard, olive tunic with cream rolled sleeves, belt, brown trousers and boots, same elevated camera and soft hand-painted shading. NO apron on the back. Always hold same axe in ANATOMICAL RIGHT HAND, which is on the SCREEN RIGHT and farther from camera in this view. Anatomical left hand SCREEN LEFT is empty. No mirrored character.
Make one natural walk IN PLACE. Equal cells, pelvis centered at same position, same scale, no body drifting or crop, no neighboring overlap.
The TWO ROWS MUST USE OPPOSITE LEADING LEGS:
TOP ROW is left-leg-leading half cycle: 1 LEFT foot planted FORWARD (toward screen upper-left), RIGHT leg extended TRAILING BACK (toward screen lower-right), as reference image1. 2 weight settles onto LEFT, trailing RIGHT heel lifts. 3 RIGHT knee raised and RIGHT boot passes next to planted LEFT ankle, feet close together. 4 RIGHT knee swings forward upper-left as LEFT stance extends.
BOTTOM ROW is right-leg-leading half cycle, NOT A REPEAT OF TOP: 5 RIGHT foot planted FORWARD (toward screen upper-left), LEFT leg extended TRAILING BACK (toward screen lower-right). The two thighs reverse overlap: left thigh and leg are now the large near leg extending down from left hip, right leg is foreshortened away. 6 weight settles onto RIGHT, trailing LEFT heel lifts. 7 LEFT knee raised and LEFT boot passes next to planted RIGHT ankle, feet close together, REVERSE of frame3. 8 LEFT knee swings forward upper-left as RIGHT stance extends, ready for frame1.
Contact figures1 and5 must have visibly exchanged front legs, and passing figures3 and7 must visibly alternate lifted knees. No eight variations of the same extended leg. Subtle bob, empty arm swings opposite to legs, axe arm restrained and always correct. Every frame faces exactly northwest AWAY from viewer, no turning. Full body and axe comfortably within each cell; generous consistent margins.
attempts.outcome: Correct northwest facing and right-hand axe, but repeats same extended right leg in most contact frames in both rows. Distinct passing3/7 insufficient to form a full alternating stride.

KEEP THIS LEG EXCHANGE VERY VISIBLE IN THE ROTATED SHEET. The top-row long trailing leg emerges below screen-LEFT hip; bottom-row long trailing leg MUST emerge below screen-RIGHT hip. Do not copy image2's same leg pose eight times.
Keep the same 4×2 layout, solid WHITE background, full figure and axe, equal scale. No new text, labels, grid or objects.
All eight bodies and heads face UPPER-LEFT AWAY FROM VIEWER like image2. Anatomical RIGHT hand (on screen right) always holds the axe, anatomical LEFT hand empty. attempts.outcome: Rotating N sheet to NW still repeats same extended leg through most contact poses; passing silhouettes weak. Rejected.
